subject: Follow-up: Reserved GPU pool fit — Fintrax initial discovery
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@fintrax.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@fintrax.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro call: inference scale & isolation needs

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for taking the intro call earlier. Wanted to capture the key points from our side so we have a shared starting point. High level: we run fraud-scoring and real-time decisioning for payments (peak TPS during end-of-month settlement windows), currently host models on a mix of self-hosted EC2 p4 instances behind an internal API gateway.

Pain points we discussed:
- Latency spikes under concurrent loads during monthly reconciles (95th pct > 450 ms)
- Cost unpredictability when we autoscale EC2 spot capacity
- Need for strict tenant isolation for cardholder and partner data (audit + encryption)
- Procurement wants predictable monthly commitments vs highly variable bills

Success criteria for any Dedicated/reserved solution:
1) Predictable throughput at 95th percentile with SLO you can quantify (target: <= 200 ms 95th for live scoring)
2) Data isolation (no co-mingled tenants; KMS integration)
3) Autoscale/burst that does not violate latency SLOs during peak windows
4) Clear runbook for failover and fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained

Ask from our side: can Redwood run a 4–6 week pilot on a reserved GPU pool that mirrors our production traffic (will provide a replay trace), and share SOC2 and encryption docs for review. Also: what baseline capacity do you recommend for a ~500 TPS sustained with 2x peak bursts to 1,200 TPS?

Attaching a rough workload worksheet we walked through (fintrax-map-of-inference-reqs.xlsx).

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of ML Ops, Fintrax
elena@fintrax.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@fintrax.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@fintrax.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call: inference scale & isolation needs

Elena — really helpful summary, thanks for sending. Recap from our side and a suggested next-step plan below.

Quick recap / alignment:
- Root cause looks like contention during your monthly reconcile windows and burst traffic patterns. Our Reserved GPU pools (dedicated tenancy) are a good fit for the isolation + predictable monthly billing you described.
- For 500 TPS sustained with 2x bursts, initial configuration we recommend: 4xA100-equivalent GPUs in a reserved pool (dedicated), with autoscale headroom for 2 additional instances for burst handling. This gives predictable baseline throughput and room to burst without changing tenancy.
- We can integrate with your KMS for keys-at-rest and produce audit logs for each request; SOC2 artifacts are available.

Proposed pilot plan (6-week):
1) Week 0: finalize SOW and sign pilot addendum (we'll send a 1-page SOW).
2) Week 1–2: sync on replay trace + baseline CI; Redwood runs a load replay against a mirrored reserved pool.
3) Week 3–5: validate latency SLOs, observe autoscale triggers and KV cache behavior; we’ll run a canary rollback scenario.
4) Week 6: pilot review and next-step recommendation (reserved commit sizing or Dedicated contract).

Immediate asks from Redwood to make sizing concrete:
- Replay trace (full week with peak window) and representative tokenization (we'll provide a small script)
- Preferred SOC2 and procurement contacts for the SOW

I've attached a starter SOW and our pilot worksheet (SOW-template-v2.docx). Suggest we lock a 30–45 minute pilot kickoff next Tue or Wed — I’m available Tue 10–11am PT or Wed 2–4pm PT.

If that schedule works, we’ll circulate the pilot SOW and a short runbook for the replay.

Thanks — looping Marcus and Monica for scoping/pilot ops.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Reserved GPU pool fit — Fintrax initial discovery

Soojin — quick internal note:
- Fintrax is price sensitive and wants predictable monthly commitment; expect procurement to push back on a long-term commit without a pilot.
- Security requirements: full KMS + per-request audit logs + ability to purge cached prompts for compliance.
- For pilot sizing, I agree with starting 4xA100-equivalent and allow 2 burst nodes; we can present pricing both as monthly reserved and an MRC with an overage band.

Monica / Alex — can you draft a trimmed SOW that includes a 6-week pilot scope (test traffic replay, success metrics: 200ms 95th, KV cache hit > 70%) and procurement SLAs? I’ll take the pricing side.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Thanks — that all looks good. We can provide a 7-day replay trace and tokenization metadata by EOD Friday. Procurement contact is Carlos (cc’d).

Two quick asks before kickoff:
1) Please share your SOC2 Type II summary and the KMS integration doc (we’ll share with our security team).
2) Can you include a short demo section in the kickoff that shows autoscale behavior under synthetic bursts? That’s important for our ops team to see how latency changes during scale-up.

I’m available for kickoff Wed 15 Sep 2026 at 10:00am PT. Carlos — can you confirm procurement availability?

Best,
Elena
